Q: Asyncio StreamReader occasionally reads 0 bytes A:

readexactly() is a picky method. From the documentation:

Read exactly n bytes. Raise an IncompleteReadError if the end of the stream is reached before n can be read, the IncompleteReadError.partial attribute of the exception contains the partial read bytes.

Since the server seems to be sending empty bytes strings sometimes, it is probably a good idea for you to put the readexactly() call on a try / except block:

try:
    first_byte = yield from reader.readexactly(1)
except asyncio.IncompleteReadError:
    pass
else:
    # Rest of your code

You could even check if you received more than 0 (zero) bytes and buffer them if your use case requires it:

except asyncio.IncompleteReadError as e:
    if len(e.partial) > 0:
        # Handle the bytes read
    else:
        pass

Q: JBoss AS 7 remote standalone client auth A:

ClientLoginModule is not currently supported on AS7 - all that login module does is associate the username and password with a thread local it does not perform any real authentication.

Regarding the InitialContext you should be seeing an exception thrown when you try and use it.

Q: What are the available approaches for binary obfuscation in iOS apps (Swift + Objective-C)? A:

Thanks for the detailed breakdown — this is very helpful.

However, regarding the LLVM-based obfuscation approach (custom LLVM passes), it seems that this is no longer practical with recent Xcode versions.

From what I’ve found:

  • Integrating custom LLVM passes into Apple’s toolchain is not officially supported

  • The older LLVM obfuscation projects are either unmaintained or incompatible with newer Xcode/Swift toolchains

  • Rebuilding or maintaining a custom toolchain for iOS development is quite complex and not feasible for most production teams

In reality, this makes the “LLVM-based obfuscation” approach more theoretical than practical for modern iOS development.

Would you say that, given the current ecosystem, most teams rely primarily on:

  • Source-level obfuscation

  • Runtime protections (anti-debugging, integrity checks)

instead of true binary-level transformations?

Curious to hear your thoughts based on real-world usage.

Q: Why use references to modify the value of a variable? A:

Now as for the code itself, it could be automatically generated. Or it has been changed multiple times over the years, and some stuff just stuck around. Both would explain why it contains parts that might seem unnecessary.

If it was hand-coded and modified over the years, then something like this should have been caught during code-review, which is why I lean towards automatic code generation tools.

Q: Minimal API issue with FromQuery A:

In your case AsParametersAttribute will do the trick:

path.MapGet("/products", async([AsParameters] ProductSearchParameters parameters, ...);

ASP.NET Core will automatically determine that corresponding properties should be mapped from query. But you can be explicit if needed too (or if automatically determined source should be changed):

public record ProductSearchParameters
(
    [FromQuery]
    string? SearchItem,
    [FromQuery]
    int Page = 1,
    [FromQuery]
    int PageSize = 20
);

See also - the Parameter Binding in Minimal API apps doc

Q: Why I'm getting 'Non-static method should not be called statically' when invoking a method in a Eloquent model? A:

If you are using one of these Laravel versions:

  • 12.0.*
  • 12.1.*
  • 12.2.*
  • 12.3.*
  • 12.4.*
  • 12.5.*:

If you get this error:

Non-static method should not be called statically

If you are calling a modern scope like this:

MyEntity::ofSomething()

If you are defining the scope like this, with the modern Laravel 12 #[Scope] annotation

<?php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Scope;

class MyEntity {

    #[Scope]
    public function ofSomething(Builder $builder): void
    {
        $builder->where('something', 1);
    }

}

Then you have a known bug, resolved in Laravel 12.6.0+. Source:

https://github.com/laravel/framework/issues/55414#issuecomment-2804600253

https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/b8f7003222eda24f150f114fe5397213b991586b

Solution

Update Laravel to 12.6.0+.

or, update like this:

-    MyEntity::ofSomething()

+    MyEntity::query()->ofSomething()
